title: Context package
description: The artifact that names exactly the knowledge one run of context resolution puts in scope. specs/0009 R1 requires the versioned schema; R2 makes the package the boundary of what may be read while it is in scope, so a consumer that needs something absent reports a gap rather than reading around it. R6 binds one package to one run — a validation failure sends the workflow back to implementation and the failed object enters the *next* resolution as a mandatory root, so a package carried across that boundary would state a scope the later attempt was never granted. specs/0009 R13 makes its persistence claim-recorded: the body recomputes from the recorded roots, the graph, the budget, and the expansion contract version, and the identity is pinned from outside the run.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects a package it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

package_id.description: specs/0009 R5: the resolution run this package was assembled for, identified so provenance runs from a decision back to the scope that informed it.

request_id.description: specs/0009 R5: the change request. specs/0001 R1 means no phase runs without one, so a package naming none is not traceable to a reason for existing.

expansion_contract_version.description: specs/0009 R17: expansion order is fixed by the contract version the package records, and a change to the order that changes which objects a package holds is a contract version change. Held apart from `contract_version` above, which versions the document: the order can move while the document shape does not, and a reader that could not tell them apart would have to guess which changed.

roots.description: specs/0009 R4: each root carries the claim that justified selecting it. Root selection is where model judgment enters resolution (specs/0005 R7), so the claim is the only thing a review has to read.

id.description: The knowledge object selected as a root.

claim.description: Why this object is in scope for this request. A root with no claim is indistinguishable from an arbitrary inclusion.

entries.description: specs/0009 R3: every object in scope, with the content hash of what was read. The hash lets a later reader establish which version a decision was made against without storing a second copy of it. Roots appear here too — a root is in scope, and a consumer checking whether it may read something should not have to consult two lists.

content_hash.description: Of the file as read, so a change to it is detectable without keeping the file.

depth.description: Edges traversed from the nearest root. Zero for a root. Recorded because a depth limit is one of the stop reasons, and a reader cannot otherwise tell which entries a lower limit would have excluded.

via.description: The edge kind that reached this entry. Absent on a root, which nothing reached.

budget.description: specs/0009 R7: the budget is stated by the caller, in a unit the package records, and the package records what was consumed against it. A framework-chosen budget would be a threshold asserted without evidence, which specs/0001 R10 forbids.

unit.description: What the limit counts. Closed so a consumer branches on a known value; `tokens` is deliberately absent until a tokenizer ships, because a unit nothing can measure is a unit nobody can honour.

depth_limit.description: Optional, and also the caller's. Absent means expansion is bounded by the closure and the budget alone.

stop_reason.description: specs/0009 R8: expansion stops for exactly one recorded reason, from this closed set, never inferred by a reader from what is present. One traversal can meet several conditions and stops on one; everything else it met is in `degradations`.

degradations.description: specs/0009 R15: recorded separately from the single stop reason, because a run that meets several conditions has several to report and one field cannot hold them. Losing all but the first is what makes the acceptance gate of specs/0001 R14 report less than what happened. R14 carries a degradation forward with the package, so a consumer reading a degraded package is told it is degraded.

code.description: specs/0009 R15's closed set. R16 fixes the correspondence with R8: the first four are the degradations specs/0001 R13 names and the last two are the truncations, `closure_complete` is the one stop reason that is never a degradation, and `unresolved_root`, `cycle`, and `contradictory_knowledge` are never stop reasons because R13 requires resolution to continue past each of them.

subject.description: What it was observed on, by identifier.

evidence.description: A structured reference to what shows it — the edge, the locator, or the pair of objects that disagree.

allOf.description: specs/0009 R16: where the stop reason is not `closure_complete`, the degradation list holds a matching entry. A truncated package reporting no degradation would say the closure was cut short and that nothing was lost.
